title: Oyfn Pripetchik
description: The Yiddish song of the little fire on the hearth, where the rabbi teaches small children their alphabet, as Susman Kisselgof's school songbook printed it, for 2 to 4 singers on Pesach Lvov's arrangement, sung in Yiddish (the words are shown in Latin letters). The first verse and the book's fourth, about the tears the children will one day find in those letters, each followed by the refrain "Zogt zhe, kinderlekh" (say it, children). Soft and moderately quick, in 3/4, as the print marks it.

licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella on Pesach Lvov's three printed voices and piano part (public domain: Lvov died 22 February 1913; the song is headed "Arrangirt fun P. Lwow" alone, while the title page says the book was worked by A. Zhitomirsky, died 1937, and P. Lvov, so any later revision of it is out of copyright too): the soprano sings the tune as printed, except that the dotted half notes ending bars 4, 8 and 12 become half notes and a beat's rest for a breath; the alto and tenor follow his two alto voices and the bass his piano's left hand, adapted for mixed voices: bar 1 the tenor on B-flat and the bass on his second alto's note; bar 2's last alto note a third higher, avoiding a leap of a sixth; bar 3 the bass on the chord's third and the alto on the root, so the duet keeps the chord's third; bars 4, 8 and 12 one chord each for the held syllable, his lead-in chords on beat 3 left out for the breath; bars 5 and 9 the alto starting a step higher, and in bar 9 on the major third, before his held note; bar 11 the alto on his second alto and the tenor on his first alto an octave down; and bar 13, where his altos sing in unison, harmonised
licence.source: tune, words and harmony from Susman Kisselgof, Lider-zamelbukh far der yidisher shul un familye (85 lider far a dreyshtimikn khor, oykh far solo, mit bagleytung fun piano; "bearbet fun A. Zhitomirski un P. Lvov" on its title page; first edition St Petersburg, 1911/12, with the Mefitse-haskole society; read from the fourth edition, "loyt der tsveyter fargreserter un farbeserter oyflage", Berlin: Juval, undated, archive.org gives [192-?]), music part p. 19, No. 13, "Der alef bejss. Arrangirt fun P. Lwow." (in Yiddish letters "fun M. Varshavski, aranzhirt fun P. Lvov"), Allegretto, M.M. 80 to the quarter, "p Messig gich", sopranos, altos I and II and piano, in G minor in 3/4, footed "Aus 'Ost und West', Redaktion Leo Winz, Berlin" and "Aufführungsrecht vorbehalten", written here in F minor at 80; verse 1 and the refrain as they are underlaid there, the fourth verse from the book's words section, p. 9, No. 13 (five verses, then verse 1 again); the words checked against M. M. Warshawsky, Yidishe folkslider (Warsaw: Aleksander Gins, 1901), pp. 13 and 14, which has kinderlekh (spelled -ליך) and gedenkt and has "Zet zhe" and "elter vern" where Kisselgof has "Zogt zhe" and "greser vern"; read from the scans at archive.org/details/nybc202667 (leaves n155 and n12) and archive.org/details/nybc204552 (leaves n14 and n15). Warshawsky died 1907, Lvov 22 February 1913, Zhitomirsky 1937, Kisselgof 1939. The Yiddish is romanized from the print in YIVO style, in standard YIVO spelling (as Oy Chanukah is): the print's German-style Latin letters respelled (j as y, sch and tsch as sh and tsh, ch as kh, ž as zh, w as v, s before a vowel as z, ss as s, ei and ej as ey, oj as oy: Ojf, schtub, heiss, bejss, Sogt že, noch, woss become Oyf, shtub, heys, beys, Zogt zhe, nokh, vos), its dialect -lach and dejnkt as standard kinderlekh and denkt (as the 1901 edition spells them), komez as komets, a-mol as a mol, its elisions kept where the notes need them (g'denkt on one note; le-rnt, fa-ye-rl split over two and three notes as the print splits le-r'nt and faj-e-r'l, and in the same way ve-rn, li-gn, tre-rn, vi-fl); in verse 2 (the book's fourth) one B-flat in bar 3 is split into two eighths for its extra syllable and "tre-" takes two notes in bar 6
